tagline: A round, spiny angler with a glowing, tasselled lure
summary: A deep-sea anglerfish shaped like a lumpy ball. Females, up to about 60 cm long, dangle a fleshy lure lit by glowing bacteria to draw prey within reach. Males are tiny, under 5 cm, and—unlike many anglerfish—they latch on only temporarily rather than fusing for life.

stats.size: Females up to about 60 cm (standard length); males about 4 cm
stats.depth: Usually 200–800 m; recorded to about 1,830 m
stats.range: Mainly the Atlantic, from Greenland and Norway to South Africa; scattered records elsewhere

facts.title: A living lantern
facts.text: The lure (esca) on the female's head 'fishing rod' glows because it hosts light-producing bacteria. In the darkness, the light draws prey within striking distance of her mouth.

facts.title: Teeth like a trap
facts.text: Its teeth point inward, so whatever swims into the mouth struggles to get back out. Recorded prey includes fishes, squids and crustaceans.

facts.title: Tiny, independent males
facts.text: Males reach only about 4 cm, against roughly 60 cm for females. In this family males apparently do not become permanently fused 'parasites' on females, as happens in some other anglerfishes.

facts.title: A temporary grip
facts.text: Males sniff out females with large nostril organs and clamp on with special bony teeth. One female carried a scar probably left by a male that later let go.

facts.title: Prey for whales
facts.text: Despite its spines, it is eaten by sperm whales: several footballfish have been found in the stomachs of whales caught off the Azores.

references.title: A Rare Deep Sea Gem Arrives at NHM (Pacific footballfish)
references.publisher: Natural History Museum of Los Angeles County

image.alt: A pale, preserved anglerfish with a rounded, lumpy body, gaping mouth and a long stalk on its head ending in a branched, tassel-like lure, against a dark background.
image.caption: A preserved female Atlantic footballfish on display at the Port of Nagoya Public Aquarium, Japan.
image.creator: KKPCW (Wikimedia Commons)

notes: Catalogue slot 'Anglerfish'. Image is the only licence-compatible Commons photo of this species: a preserved museum specimen labelled 'チョウチンアンコウ' (the Japanese standard name for H. groenlandicus) at the Port of Nagoya Public Aquarium, filed in Category:Himantolophus groenlandicus; ID rests on the aquarium label. Lure-bacteria and inward-teeth facts are from NHM LA describing the family (Pacific footballfish, H. sagamius) and apply to footballfishes generally; male non-parasitism is stated for this species by FishBase ('apparently') and for the family by NHM. Wikipedia used for range, diet, temporary-attachment and Azores sperm-whale records (it cites Pietsch 2009, Oceanic Anglerfishes). Distribution: FishBase lists 'tropical and temperate parts of all oceans' while Wikipedia/IUCN emphasise the Atlantic; editor may wish to verify. Note: the familiar 'ball-shaped anglerfish with lantern' image in Japan (chōchin-ankō) refers to this species.
